title: Zolotarev–Frobenius for EVERY odd modulus: sign(x ↦ a·x on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for all odd n
description: The capstone of the elementary-Zolotarev program. For EVERY odd n > 0, a unit a : (ℤ/n)ˣ, and any integer representative A ≡ a (mod n), the sign of the multiplication-by-a permutation of the WHOLE ring ℤ/n (ZolotarevCRT.ringMulPerm a) equals the Jacobi symbol J(A | n). This is the full Frobenius (1914) generalization of Zolotarev's lemma — valid for ALL odd moduli, not merely the squarefree ones (parent oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01) nor merely the prime powers (parent oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01). It performs the final assembly the whole-ring prime-power lemma explicitly flagged: 'Together with the CRT decomposition sign_ringMulPerm_crt and jacobiSym.mul_right, this yields the Frobenius/Zolotarev identity for every odd n — completing the program the squarefree-odd lemma began.' The proof is a multiplicative induction on n (Nat.recOnPosPrimePosCoprime): the n = 1 case is trivial (ℤ/1 is a point); the prime-power case n = pᵉ (p odd, since pᵉ is odd) is the whole-ring prime-power identity, repackaged in representative-free form using that legendreSym p factors through ℤ/p; and the coprime case n = u·v feeds the SAME numerator A to both factors through the CRT multiplicativity sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd, matching jacobiSym.mul_right J(A | u·v) = J(A | u)·J(A | v). The even modulus 2ⁿ is genuinely excluded — there ℤ/2ⁿ has even cardinality (the sign degenerates) and the Jacobi symbol is undefined for even denominators.

overview.text: Three layers of the gallery now combine into one statement. The CRT decomposition (great-great-grandparent oq-01-oq-03) showed the multiplication-permutation sign on ℤ/n factors, through the Chinese Remainder isomorphism, as a product over coprime factors, and is genuinely multiplicative when the factors are odd. The whole-ring prime-power lemma (parent oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01) computed the sign on each ℤ/pᵉ to be J(a | pᵉ). Multiplicative induction on n glues them: every odd n is built from 1 by repeatedly taking a coprime product or a prime power, and the Zolotarev sign tracks the Jacobi symbol at each step, exactly as J does. The only care needed is bookkeeping of the numerator: the Jacobi symbol J(A | n) depends on the integer A only through A mod n, so the proof threads a single representative A through the whole induction and lets the cast hypotheses (A : ℤ/m) = (a₁ : ℤ/m) at each coprime factor follow from one application of map_intCast.
overview.historicalContext: Zolotarev (1872) identified the Legendre symbol (a/p) with the sign of x ↦ ax on (ℤ/p)ˣ and used it to prove the quadratic reciprocity law. Frobenius (1914) generalized this to composite moduli and the Jacobi symbol: the sign of x ↦ ax on ℤ/n is J(a | n) for every odd n. The gallery rebuilt the Frobenius theorem from elementary pieces in layers — prime base case (oq-01-oq-03-oq-01), CRT decomposition (oq-01-oq-03), squarefree-odd induction (oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01), units-level prime power (oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01), whole-ring prime power (oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01) — each layer flagging the next obstruction. This entry removes the last one and states the theorem in its full generality.
overview.problemStatement: Open Question (the listed follow-up of elementary-quadratic-reciprocity-oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01): combine the per-prime-power identity sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/pᵉ) = J(a | pᵉ) with the CRT multiplicativity sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd and jacobiSym.mul_right to obtain sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for EVERY odd n. This entry proves exactly that, for every odd n > 0, unit a : (ℤ/n)ˣ, and representative A ≡ a (mod n).
overview.proofStrategy: Part I (bridges): coe_unitsMap relates the underlying element of ZMod.unitsMap h u to the cast of u; chineseRemainder_fst / chineseRemainder_snd identify the two CRT projections with the casts to ℤ/m and ℤ/n (forced by RingHom.ext_zmod, since any two ring homs out of ℤ/(m·n) agree); legendreSym_congr shows legendreSym p A depends on A only through A mod p (legendreSym.mod + ZMod.intCast_eq_intCast_iff). Part II (prime-power base, representative-free): sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym_of_cast repackages the parent's sign_ringMulPerm_eq_legendre_pow and jacobiSym_prime_pow into sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/pᵏ) = J(A | pᵏ) for any A ≡ a (mod pᵏ), reducing the two legendre symbols to the same residue mod p via legendreSym_congr. Part III (induction): main_aux runs Nat.recOnPosPrimePosCoprime. The zero case is excluded by NeZero; the one case uses Subsingleton (ℤ/1) and jacobiSym.one_right; the prime_pow case derives p ≠ 2 from Odd (pᵏ) (Nat.even_pow / Nat.odd_iff) and applies Part II; the coprime case n = u·v takes a₁ = unitsMap a, a₂ = unitsMap a, proves the CRT component and numerator-cast hypotheses, applies sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd to split the sign, the two inductive hypotheses to identify each factor with J(A | u), J(A | v), and jacobiSym.mul_right to recombine.
keyInsights: Multiplicativity of the Jacobi symbol in its denominator is not an extra number-theoretic input: it is the permutation-level shadow of the Chinese Remainder Theorem (sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd), and the whole induction simply has the Zolotarev sign and the Jacobi symbol take the same value at each multiplicative building block.

Multiplicative induction (Nat.recOnPosPrimePosCoprime) is the exact shape of the argument: every odd n is assembled from 1 by coprime products and prime powers, the two non-trivial cases are precisely the two lemmas already proved (prime-power base, CRT multiplicativity), and oddness propagates to every factor (Nat.odd_mul, Nat.even_pow).

Threading a single integer representative A through the induction — rather than recomputing a canonical residue at each modulus — keeps the bookkeeping trivial: J(A | n) depends only on A mod n, the CRT cast hypotheses (A : ℤ/m) = (a₁ : ℤ/m) reduce to map_intCast, and the prime-power base only needs A mod p.

Any two ring homomorphisms out of ℤ/(m·n) coincide (RingHom.ext_zmod), so the CRT projections are forced to be the canonical casts — no need to unfold the definition of ZMod.chineseRemainder to match its components against ZMod.unitsMap.

The even modulus is excluded for a real reason, not a technical one: on ℤ/2ⁿ the cardinality is even so the sign character degenerates, and the Jacobi symbol J(· | 2ⁿ) is not even defined. The theorem is exactly as general as the Jacobi symbol itself.
prerequisites: The CRT multiplicativity ZolotarevCRT.sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd and the whole-ring multiplication permutation ZolotarevCRT.ringMulPerm
Multiplicative induction on ℕ (Nat.recOnPosPrimePosCoprime) and oddness of factors (Nat.odd_mul, Nat.even_pow, Nat.odd_iff)
ZMod reduction maps ZMod.castHom / ZMod.unitsMap, uniqueness of ring homs out of ZMod (RingHom.ext_zmod), and ZMod.chineseRemainder
Jacobi-symbol multiplicativity and base cases (jacobiSym.mul_right, jacobiSym.one_right), and legendreSym.mod / ZMod.intCast_eq_intCast_iff

sections.title: Generic bridges: units reduction, CRT components, legendreSym congruence
sections.content: coe_unitsMap: (ZMod.unitsMap h u : ℤ/m) = castHom h (u : ℤ/n). chineseRemainder_fst / chineseRemainder_snd: the two projections of ZMod.chineseRemainder are the canonical casts to ℤ/m and ℤ/n — proved by RingHom.ext_zmod (any two ring homs out of ℤ/(m·n) are equal). legendreSym_congr: equal residues mod p give equal Legendre symbols (legendreSym.mod + ZMod.intCast_eq_intCast_iff).

sections.title: The prime-power base in representative-free form
sections.content: sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym_of_cast: for an odd prime p, k ≥ 1, a unit a : (ℤ/pᵏ)ˣ and any integer A ≡ a (mod pᵏ), sign(ringMulPerm a) = J(A | pᵏ). Repackages the parent's sign_ringMulPerm_eq_legendre_pow and jacobiSym_prime_pow, reducing both legendre symbols (of (a mod p).val and of A) to the same residue mod p via legendreSym_congr and one cast of the hypothesis A ≡ a down to ℤ/p.

sections.title: Multiplicative induction over the odd modulus
sections.content: main_aux: Nat.recOnPosPrimePosCoprime. zero excluded by NeZero; one is ℤ/1 trivial (jacobiSym.one_right); prime_pow derives p ≠ 2 from Odd (pᵏ) and applies the base; coprime n = u·v takes a₁, a₂ = unitsMap a, proves the CRT-component and numerator-cast hypotheses, splits the sign by sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd, applies both inductive hypotheses, and recombines with jacobiSym.mul_right.

sections.title: The full odd-modulus Zolotarev–Frobenius identity
sections.content: sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym_odd: for every odd n > 0, unit a, and representative A ≡ a (mod n), sign(ringMulPerm a) = J(A | n). sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym_val: the canonical-representative form J((a).val | n). signRingHom_eq_jacobiSym: through ZolotarevCRT.signRingHom, the Zolotarev sign CHARACTER on (ℤ/n)ˣ IS the Jacobi symbol for odd n.

meta.author: Zolotarev (1872), Frobenius (1914)
meta.assumptions: None. The file has 0 axiom declarations, 0 sorries, no native_decide, and no assumption-carrying structures. The headline theorems sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym_odd, sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym_val and signRingHom_eq_jacobiSym were checked with #print axioms and depend only on propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound (the standard foundational axioms, which do not count as assumptions). This completes the elementary-Zolotarev program: sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for every odd n > 0. The even modulus 2ⁿ is genuinely outside scope — the Jacobi symbol is undefined for even denominators.

conclusion.summary: Proves, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, the full Frobenius/Zolotarev identity for EVERY odd modulus: for any odd n > 0, a unit a : (ℤ/n)ˣ, and any integer representative A ≡ a (mod n), the sign of multiplication-by-a on the whole ring ℤ/n equals the Jacobi symbol J(A | n). It is a multiplicative induction (Nat.recOnPosPrimePosCoprime) gluing the two lemmas the lineage had isolated: the whole-ring prime-power identity (each ℤ/pᵉ factor) and the CRT multiplicativity sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd (coprime products), with the Jacobi symbol's own multiplicativity jacobiSym.mul_right mirroring the latter step. A single integer representative A is threaded through the induction, so all numerator bookkeeping reduces to map_intCast and legendreSym.mod.
conclusion.implications: Completes the elementary reconstruction of the Frobenius generalization of Zolotarev's lemma: the Zolotarev sign character on (ℤ/n)ˣ IS the Jacobi symbol for all odd n (signRingHom_eq_jacobiSym), from which the quadratic reciprocity law follows by Zolotarev's original shuffle-permutation argument. The reusable by-products are coe_unitsMap, the forced-cast characterization of the CRT projections (chineseRemainder_fst / chineseRemainder_snd via RingHom.ext_zmod), and the representative-free prime-power base.
openQuestions: Specialize the general-odd Frobenius identity to recover the quadratic reciprocity law (a/p)(p/a) = (-1)^… directly via the sign of a suitable shuffle permutation, as in Zolotarev's 1872 derivation.
Promote chineseRemainder_fst / chineseRemainder_snd to standalone Mathlib-style simp lemmas characterizing the projections of ZMod.chineseRemainder as the canonical casts.
Recover the supplementary laws (a = -1 and a = 2) for odd n as values of signRingHom, completing the dictionary between permutation signs on ℤ/n and the full Jacobi symbol.

crossReferences.note: The whole-ring prime-power identity sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/pⁿ) = J(a | pⁿ); this entry performs the every-odd-n assembly it explicitly flagged, using it as the prime-power case of the induction.
Defines ZolotarevCRT.ringMulPerm and proves the CRT multiplicativity sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd that supplies the coprime-product step of the induction.
The squarefree-odd Frobenius/Zolotarev identity; this entry strictly generalizes it from squarefree odd n to ALL odd n by adding the prime-power factors.
